title: PulseQuarry throughput validation and customer acceptance
creator: Marcus Li
description: Build and iterate PulseQuarry: a tenant-aware, scenario-driven throughput validation harness and a packaged customer acceptance runbook for Dedicated capacity. Goal: provide reproducible signatures for SLA verification, realistic tail-latency stress profiles, and a concise acceptance script customers can run during onboarding.
acceptance_criteria: PulseQuarry can replay customer-like mixes (ramp, sustain, burst) with <5% variance in 95th percentile tail-latency across runs on same fleet
Produce per-tenant throughput signatures and a summary PDF suitable for customer signoff
Include automated detection of autoscaler policy regressions (scaling misfires or oscillations) and generate actionable alerts
Acceptance runbook includes step-by-step commands, expected outputs, and fallback guidance for common failure modes
test_plan: Develop small-footprint driver that can emulate 10k concurrent short-chat requests and 500 long-generation requests with configurable token distributions
Implement request classification and weighting so each test can model mixes: interactive (latency-sensitive), batch (throughput-first), and KV-heavy (cache-sensitive)
Add built-in measurement hooks for per-request token cost, KV cache hit ratio, batch sizes, and GPU utilization
Run triage matrix across 3 fleet sizes and 2 autoscale policies (reactive vs predictive) to compare tail-latency and throughput headroom
Create deterministic seed mode and workspace snapshot feature so customers can reproduce runs locally or in our environment
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Spike completed — basic harness prototype can generate sustained 1k rps of short messages against a single Dedicated node (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/pulsequarry/pull/12)
2025-02-20: Measurement schema finalized; added KV cache and batch size metrics to the driver telemetry. Draft Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood/workspaces/dedicated/pulsequarry-spec
2025-02-27: First multi-tenant scenario run across a 4-node pool. Observed autoscaler overshoot when burst ratio >3x sustained load; created ENG-721010 to track fix
2025-03-02: Customer acceptance script draft reviewed by SEs and Solutions (feedback: simplify CLI flags, add preflight checks). Incorporated feedback and published CLI v0.2
2025-03-04: Canary onboarding with internal alpha customer scheduled for 2025-03-12; will exercise canary autoscale policy and capture signoff artifacts
risks: Driver-induced measurement noise: need CPU-isolation for driver hosts to avoid polluting latency numbers
Autoscaler interplay: creating synthetic bursts can trigger safety mechanisms and obscure true capacity limits unless we model tenant elasticity correctly
Customer reproducibility: customers with different networking/K8s setups may see different results; must provide a narrow preflight checklist
Security: harness will require controlled credentials to Dedicated endpoints — ensure we provide ephemeral keys and scoped access
decisions: Use gRPC for driver->agent telemetry to minimize JSON parsing overhead and keep telemetry high-fidelity
Expose a single 'scenario' DSL (YAML) for customers to declare mixes instead of requiring custom scripts
Package acceptance runbook as a one-click job in Console and a CLI wrapper for advanced users
next_steps: Finish autoscaler regression detector (ENG-721010) and add to PulseQuarry alert rules
Finalize customer-facing acceptance PDF and CLI usage examples by 2025-03-10
Run alpha onboarding with internal customer; capture artifacts and iterate on runbook
Coordinate with Solutions on training materials and support checklist
